title: Research consent: pressure on the reviewer
decision: May the protocol be offered as written, or should it be redesigned, deferred or refused?

facts.text: Identifiable records create a disclosed meaningful privacy risk; no numerical estimate is stipulated.
Participants understand the disclosed terms and may ask questions and decline.
Ordinary care and existing entitlements are unaffected by refusal.
Research benefit is uncertain; a less identifiable design is feasible but less informative; redesign has delay costs.
A senior director asks the reviewer to approve promptly; no explicit threat or reward is stipulated.

alternatives.description: Require the less identifiable design, accepting reduced information and delay.
Defer or refuse, specifying the unmet condition and costs.

replaces.text: Declining participants must wait four additional weeks for the same ordinary care; other existing entitlements are unchanged.

participant_option_overrides.ordinary_care_access: Same ordinary care, with four additional weeks of waiting following refusal.

unknowns: Which grounds and safeguards justify the burdens
source_scope: All case facts are invented; existing MORARG consent sources provide questions and principles, not evidence for this scenario.

participant_options.ordinary_care_access: Usual schedule; participation is additional and does not improve the ordinary-care entitlement.
Usual schedule; refusal has no additional wait in the baseline.
